subject: Aligning incident triage playbook with OKRs — QBR prep and SLA decision log
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: (none)
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aligning incident triage playbook with OKRs — QBR prep and SLA decision log

Team —

Attached is the postmortem summary and a proposed incident triage playbook tweak after the July 30 ACME incident. Key points up front:

- Root cause: KV cache warmup + noisy background syncs on a subset of Dedicated hosts; sustained tail latency produced at-scale SLO violations for 18 minutes.
- Impact: customer-facing latency spikes affecting ~1.2% of requests for a 45-min window; ACME observed a 9% reduction in successful inference throughput during peak.
- Immediate remediation taken: bypassed background syncs, forced cache priming for warm hosts, emergency scaling policy triggered.

Attachments included: incident-timeline-ACME-20270730.pdf (chronology + minimal logs), sla-decision-log.xlsx (draft decision log with recommended SLA changes and owners).

For QBR slides we need two asks from leadership:
1) Decision on temporary SLA window change for Dedicated customers impacted by cache-warmup anomalies (Proposal A in sheet: 95th->97th baseline for 2 quarters with rollback review).
2) Approval for the proposed runbook changes and two immediate hires/contractors to own the cache/telemetry workstream (owners suggested in the sheet).

Please reply with: one-line decision (approve/adjust/reject) for each ask and a named owner for the runbook implementation by EOD Wednesday so we can finalize QBR material.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: incident-timeline-ACME-20270730.pdf, sla-decision-log.xlsx
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning incident triage playbook with OKRs — QBR prep and SLA decision log

Thanks Marissa — high level looks good. Two quick clarifying asks before I sign off on anything for the QBR:

- Can you provide a concise 3-bullet tradeoff per option in the SLA sheet (i.e., impact on revenue/CSAT, implementation effort, rollback trigger)? I want to put one slide of tradeoffs in the exec packet.
- For the hire/contractor ask, give me the minimum viable scope and timeline to remove the single point of regression (cache warmup); do not include broad hiring asks — we can expand later if needed.

If you can get that to me by EOD Tuesday I will draft the leadership note for the QBR. If Hannah or Laura think there are better alternatives, mark them up inline and ping me.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
CEO, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning incident triage playbook with OKRs — QBR prep and SLA decision log

On Mon, Aug 9, 2027 at 9:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Attached is the postmortem summary and a proposed incident triage playbook tweak after the July 30 ACME incident....

Quick markups inline and a recommended short decision rubric below. I focused on keeping alignment with this quarter's Reliability OKRs (reduce customer-perceived SLO breaches by 40% and decrease MTTI by 20%).

Recommendation (3-bullet tradeoff per option for slide):
- Proposal A (temp 95th->97th baseline for 2 quarters): Pros: eases immediate QBR optics and reduces near-term churn risk; Cons: masks tail issues from product teams; Implementation: low (policy change + communication); Rollback trigger: when 95th improved 25% from baseline for two consecutive weeks.
- Proposal B (no SLA change, urgent fix + credits): Pros: maintains fidelity of SLOs; Cons: customer dissatisfaction risk and higher near-term credit cost; Implementation: medium (engineer + ops work); Rollback trigger: post-implementation validation of KV warmup mitigation across clusters.
- Proposal C (targeted exception for impacted Dedicated customers only): Pros: surgical, minimizes broad promise change; Cons: operational complexity for billing and comms; Implementation: medium-high.

Minimum viable scope for the cache warmup fix (for hire/contractor ask):
- 6-week contractor to implement deterministic cache-priming and telemetry hooks on warm paths, test across canary regions, and hand off runbooks. Owner: Hannah Schmitt (SRE) with 0.2 Product support (Marissa).

Suggested owner matrix (for QBR):
- Decision authority (SLA window): Vivek
- Implementation owner (cache fix): Hannah Schmitt
- Customer comms + credits: Laura Bennett (Sales/CS lead)

I updated sla-decision-log.xlsx with the rubric and owners (see tab 'Leadership_Decision_Rubric').

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Site Reliability Engineering
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@acme-cloud.com>, procurement@acme-cloud.com
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning incident triage playbook with OKRs — QBR prep and SLA decision log

Vivek / Team —

Thanks for the quick turn. Per Vivek's ask and Hannah's rubric, I'm confirming the leadership decisions to include in the QBR packet:

1) SLA decision: APPROVE Proposal C — targeted exception for impacted Dedicated accounts (Acme Cloud included) for one quarter, with a billing reconciliation plan and a technical rollback trigger defined in the decision log.
2) Implementation hire: APPROVE 6-week contractor to execute deterministic cache-priming and telemetry instrumentation as defined in Hannah's scope. Owner: Hannah Schmitt.

Next steps I executed:
- Updated sla-decision-log.xlsx with final language and sign-off column.
- Drafted customer comms for ACME and attached a redline (see attachments). Laura will follow up with Sean/procurement to schedule a short 1:1 tomorrow morning to align on credits and timeline.
- Added a QBR slide deck stub in the Drive folder (link below) with a 1-slide summary and 1-slide timeline.

If there are no objections by EOD tomorrow I'll publish the decision log and lock the QBR slides for exec review.

Laura Bennett
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
